proposals.evidence: Turner 12278 śatá '100' explicitly cites European Romani šel. The source prints Zargari śel 'one hundred' in its numeral table (p. 137 §3.5.1) and explains the -i- connector before following numerals (p. 138 §3.5.1.1). This is the simple hundred stem. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

proposals.evidence: The source prints duy-śel 'two hundred' (p. 138 §3.5.1) and explicitly states that numerals are compounded (§3.5.1.1). Its two source components are attested duy 'two' (already linked to CDIAL 6648) and śel 'hundred' (newly linked to CDIAL 12278). The component edge records this composition, not a separate whole-word Sanskrit ancestor. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

This records components, not a single ancient compound etymon. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.
